title.en: Deformable prop with a construction-aware support cage

summary: Organize a soft prop around a low-complexity cage, protected openings, attachment zones and thickness checks so expressive deformation does not silently destroy construction.
objective: Across approved extreme poses, the prop keeps intentional openings clear, attachments seated, wall thickness visually credible and deformation ownership explicit after export.
applies_when: A bag, cushion, soft container, padded part or stylized flexible prop deforms as a coordinated volume rather than through a skeletal limb hierarchy.
intent_signals: bend a bag without collapsing the zipper
example_prompts: Create a soft equipment pouch whose zipper opening and strap anchors remain readable while the body squashes.
Build a stylized cushion with piping and buttons that follows one low-resolution deformation cage.
negative_signals: Claim the cage automatically preserves volume
Bind after moving source and cage into unrelated poses
Export a Blender modifier expecting Three.js to evaluate it
not_for: An articulated character limb better represented by joints and skinning.

principles: The cage is a control envelope, not a physical solver. Its shape and weights determine broad motion; construction checks decide whether thickness, openings and attachments remain acceptable.

Separate soft body regions from protected zones. An opening rim, rigid insert, buckle seat or handle root may need reduced influence, a dedicated inner cage or explicit child transform rather than unrestricted deformation.
Design rest and extreme poses together. A prop that looks coherent only at rest has not established a deformation archetype.
implementation: Model outer shell, inner opening/rim, seams or piping, and attachment hardware as named parts. Give exposed openings actual depth or paired surfaces when the intended camera can see inside.

Create a simple closed cage around the deforming region with outward normals and enough control faces near openings and anchors. Bind Mesh Deform in the agreed rest state; use vertex groups to restrict influence and increase precision only when the comparison justifies it.

For attachments that must follow without bending, parent a rigid part to a named helper driven from a stable cage region or use a separate deformation mask. Do not bake a connector into the shell and then animate a second unrelated transform.

Author representative bend, squash and twist poses. At each pose, measure or visually compare the narrowest opening, minimum wall separation, attachment penetration and silhouette; revise cage topology or influence rather than hiding failure with shading.

Choose the transport owner: export a fixed evaluated pose, bake approved poses as topology-compatible morph targets, or rig a runtime deformation representation. glTF and Three.js do not receive the editable Mesh Deform cage operation itself.
Store an undeformed rest snapshot and reset all morph, skin or controller weights together with attachment transforms.
observable_checks: At every approved pose, the zipper, mouth or handle opening remains intentionally open and its rim does not cross itself.
Outer and inner surfaces do not visibly invert or intersect at the tightest bend; a thickness probe at declared landmarks stays above the authored visual minimum.
Rigid attachments remain seated without sinking into or floating away from their anchor regions.
The exported runtime representation reproduces the approved rest and extreme silhouettes, and reset returns exactly to the stored rest state.

creative_affordances: Use asymmetric squash, folded corners or exaggerated rebound for character while protecting functional openings.
Expose the low-resolution cage as an inspection overlay in educational or tooling views.
known_limits: Cage deformation does not conserve volume, enforce collisions, preserve a numerical thickness or predict material response.
Morph or skin transport imposes its own topology and ownership contracts.
Authored reusable guidance; no cage bind, export or runtime artifact was executed for this record.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5's Mesh Deform modifier uses an arbitrary closed mesh as a cage around another mesh, requires binding to map current cage and object vertices, can restrict affected vertices with a vertex group, and provides precision and dynamic-binding controls; the manual also requires outward cage normals for inside/outside determination.
claims.scope: Documented Blender Mesh Deform authoring behavior; it does not claim physical simulation or automatic preservation of openings, volume or thickness.
